newsitem.title: CHINA: HK stocks seen continuing rebound, upside limited.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks seen continuing rebound, upside limited.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks are expected to continue their rebound on Friday but the upside should be limited due to a lack of solid good news, brokers said.

Before it reversed course on Thursday, the Hang Seng Index had fallen about 400 point since Hong Kong returned to Chinese rule on July 1, said Andrew To, dealing director at OSK Asia Securities. "The rebound should continue on Friday," he said.
The Hang Seng Index closed 135.50 points, or 0.92 percent, higher at 14,839.23 on Thursday.
"The blue chip index is likely to move up 50-100 points since there is no concrete news to push it further," To said.
Overnight, the Hang Seng London Reference Index added 12.03 points to finish at 14,851.26.
"Red chips have stablised following a brief correction and they are seen tending higher, but trading overall should move sideway," said Edwin Cheung, dealing director at Taiwan Securities.

There was big selling pressure near the 15,000 level on the Hang Seng Index since the market was uncertain about what measures the government would announce in October to curb high property prices, Cheung said.
